scope: Proposition 7.4 (Nonidentity on every algebraic branch) of the manuscript “Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2” (preprints/Elliptic-Squares-and-Zilber-Pink-for-Curves-in-A2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3ecf115570d0b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every group selected in Proposition 6.5, every irreducible closed algebraic W containing its target and having nonconstant a, and every normalized branch over the generic point of a component of W ∩ {a = 0}, at least one of its equations is a nonzero germ on that branch. This holds for each of the three types (1), (2), and (3), with their base-coordinate equations included.
